battle.name: 第一次粵桂戰爭
battle.brief: 維基百科「戰爭列表」所列第一次粵桂戰爭，是1920年廣東與廣西軍閥勢力為爭奪區域主導權而爆發的交鋒。參戰軍隊沿用1840年已列裝的雷管步槍（Percussion rifle），反映當時軍隊仍以早期火藥槍械作為步兵裝備。

kit.name: 雷管步槍
kit.history: 雷管步槍是法軍十九世紀中期採用的制式地面步槍，配置於步兵單位，作為日常訓練與作戰所用的一般槍械，構成當時軍隊步兵體系的核心裝備。

countries: 本役的交戰主體是中華民國廣東軍與中華民國廣西軍，而不是兩個對外宣告獨立的國家。廣東軍以陳炯明為實際統帥，依省軍各師、獨立旅及炮兵部隊作戰，控制廣州、西江下游與粵北通道；廣西舊桂軍以陸榮廷為最高統帥，依托桂東、桂中、桂南的省軍系統防守，兵力可由南寧、柳州、桂林與梧州互相策應。兩軍形式上同屬中華民國，北京政府卻沒有能力把粵桂兩省統一編入同一戰役指揮部，命令、糧餉與武器補充實際上均由地方軍事首長決定。沈鴻英、林虎所領的新桂系起初隸屬廣西方面，中途反陸並與陳炯明合作，因此是廣西內部的第三支政治軍力，不是第三個國家。整個戰區由廣州後方、西江下游、梧州門戶及桂東走廊串聯；沿海與江上船隻主要負責運輸，沒有可靠史料足以把海軍艦炮列為決定勝負的武器。
countriesEn: The principal belligerents in this campaign were the Guangdong Army and the Guangxi Army of the Republic of China, not two internationally recognized sovereign states. The Guangdong Army, under the effective command of Chen Jiongming, fought with provincial divisions, independent brigades, and artillery units, controlling Guangzhou, the lower Xijiang River, and the northern approaches to Guangdong. The old Guangxi clique army, headed by Lu Rongting, relied on provincial formations distributed across eastern, central, and southern Guangxi, with mutual support planned among Nanning, Liuzhou, Guilin, and Wuzhou. Both armies formally belonged to the Republic of China, but the government in Beijing could not combine the two provinces under an effective operational command; orders, pay, and resupply remained under local military control. Shen Hongying and Lin Hu originally belonged to the Guangxi side, but their New Guangxi clique later revolted against Lu and cooperated with Chen, making it a third internal Guangxi politico-military force rather than a foreign ally. The operational region linked Guangzhou, the lower Xijiang, the gateway at Wuzhou, and the corridors of eastern Guangxi. Coastal and river vessels were principally used for transport, and the surviving evidence does not justify treating naval gunfire as a decisive weapon in the campaign.
people: 陳炯明在一九二〇年的身分是廣東省的實際軍事首長，粵軍各師、旅及炮兵名義上均受他節制。他能決定西江防線、桂東進攻方向及與新桂系合作的政治條件，但其軍隊來自不同省軍系統，裝備、糧餉和忠誠程度並不一致，不能按現代制式軍的集中指揮能力估算。陸榮廷時任廣西督軍，是舊桂系的最高政治與軍事領袖，既要守住桂系原有的省政位置，也要維持桂林、柳州、南寧至梧州的防禦縱深。沈鴻英與林虎都是廣西本地軍政人物，兩人對陸榮廷的統治與軍隊安排不滿，遂利用粵桂衝突在廣西內部舉兵；其作用不是替陳炯明提供一支普通援軍，而是切斷桂軍後方，使陸的指揮體系迅速失去完整。孫中山當時並不在本役前線，也不是粵軍的戰場指揮者。各次局部戰鬥的師、旅番號及前線指揮官，在不同回憶錄與戰報中常有差異，因此不能把每一場戰鬥硬歸給一名將領。可以確定的核心關係，是陳炯明代表粵軍、陸榮廷代表舊桂軍、沈鴻英與林虎代表桂軍內部倒陸的一支力量。
peopleEn: In 1920, Chen Jiongming was the effective military head of Guangdong. The provincial divisions, brigades, and artillery of the Guangdong Army formally acknowledged his command. He could determine the defense of the Xijiang, the direction of operations in eastern Guangxi, and the political terms of cooperation with the New Guangxi clique. His forces nevertheless came from different provincial formations and varied considerably in equipment, pay, and loyalty, so they should not be assessed as if they possessed the centralized command capabilities of a modern regular army. Lu Rongting, then governor and military governor of Guangxi, was the supreme political and military leader of the old Guangxi clique. He had to preserve the clique’s existing control of provincial government while maintaining the defensive depth linking Guilin, Liuzhou, Nanning, and Wuzhou. Shen Hongying and Lin Hu were native Guangxi military-political figures who were dissatisfied with Lu’s rule and arrangements. They used the Guangdong-Guangxi confrontation to rise within Guangxi itself. Their contribution was not simply that of an ordinary reinforcement for Chen: their revolt opened the Guangxi rear and rapidly deprived Lu’s command of cohesion. Sun Yat-sen was not on this battlefield and did not command the Guangdong forces. Accounts differ over the brigade and division designations and local commanders attached to individual actions, so it would be unsafe to assign every engagement to one named general. The firmly established central relationship was Chen for the Guangdong Army, Lu for the old Guangxi clique, and Shen and Lin for the Guangxi faction that turned against Lu.
kits: 雙方的主要作戰裝備集中在七九二乘五七毫米步槍、機槍與七五毫米炮兵。步槍可核對的主要型號包括漢陽八八式步槍，即 Hanyang Type 88，以及德國 Gewehr 88；兩者均使用七九二乘五七毫米彈，後膛閉鎖結構相同，但各師的槍況、附件和備件供應並不一致。機槍包括英製 Maxim M1909 重機槍與法製 Hotchkiss M1909 輕機槍，前者以水冷方式和彈帶供彈，後者採輕便機架與magazine供彈，兩者均可使用七九二乘五七毫米彈。炮兵以七五毫米野戰炮和山炮為核心，可確定的型號包括法製 Schneider-Creusot Mle 1917 七五毫米山炮；各支省軍還混有來源不同的七五炮，不能把所有火炮一概記成同一製造系統。炮彈包括榴彈與高爆彈，步槍及機槍則依賴不同批次、不同包裝的七九二毫米彈藥。西江與桂東沒有連續鐵路，內河汽艇、淺底駁船、騾馬和步兵背架因此構成主要運輸系統。戰區沒有能左右攻守的裝甲力量，也沒有可信記錄顯示航空隊曾發揮決定性作用；所有列出的武器型號在一九二〇年以前均已列裝。
kitsEn: The principal combat equipment of both sides consisted of 7.92 × 57 mm rifles, machine guns, and 75 mm artillery. The principal identifiable rifle types were the Chinese Hanyang Type 88 and the German Gewehr 88. Both used the 7.92 × 57 mm cartridge and the same bolt-action operating principle, although ammunition, spare parts, and the condition of individual weapons varied from formation to formation. Machine guns included the British Maxim M1909 heavy machine gun and the French Hotchkiss M1909 light machine gun. The Maxim used a water-cooling system and belt feed, while the Hotchkiss used a comparatively portable mount and magazine feed; both were capable of firing 7.92 × 57 mm ammunition. Artillery centered on 75 mm field and mountain guns, with the French Schneider-Creusot Mle 1917 75 mm mountain gun among the models that can be positively identified. Provincial formations also operated 75 mm pieces from different sources, so every gun cannot responsibly be assigned to a single manufacturing system. Artillery ammunition included shrapnel and high-explosive rounds, while rifles and machine guns depended on 7.92 mm ammunition obtained in different lots and packings. There was no continuous railway through the Xijiang or eastern Guangxi, so river motorboats, shallow-draft barges, pack animals, and infantry carrying equipment formed the main transport system. No armored force capable of deciding the campaign operated in the theater, and no reliable evidence shows that aviation had a decisive role. Every weapon model named here had entered service before 1920.
tactics: 戰役初期，粵軍依托西江下游道路與渡口建立防線，桂軍則利用桂東、桂中山地控制通往梧州、平樂、桂林和柳州的道路。進攻時，七五炮先用於壓制道路交叉點和河岸陣地，Maxim M1909等重機槍占據路口、橋頭及制高點，Hotchkiss M1909則跟隨步兵前進，以較高射速封鎖接近道路；山炮受地形和運力限制，不能像平射炮那樣對縱深目標持續射擊。粵軍越過西江後，不只沿一條道路直推，而是利用水路由梧州接運部隊，再由賀縣、平樂方向展開，使桂軍必須同時封住東線與南寧後方。桂軍依托村落、山隘和道路節點進行抵抗，避免在開闊地接受完整火力，但這種分散防守也使各旅不易集中。決定戰局變化的並非一次正面殲滅，而是沈鴻英、林虎在廣西內部的起兵：粵軍在正面施加壓力，新桂系則奪取南寧及後方機關，使陸榮廷無法集中兵力。兩軍都受制於長距離通信、前線指揮分散和多種軍械並存；前線常以傳令、軍報和後方電報協調，命令傳遞速度不足以支撐大規模連續攻勢，因此戰役整體呈現流動戰而非固定塹壕戰。
tacticsEn: At the beginning of the campaign, the Guangdong Army established a defensive line along roads and ferry crossings on the lower Xijiang. The Guangxi Army used the mountainous terrain of eastern and central Guangxi to control the routes toward Wuzhou, Pingle, Guilin, and Liuzhou. During attacks, 75 mm guns were used to suppress road junctions and riverbank positions; Maxim M1909 heavy machine guns occupied road bends, bridgeheads, and commanding ground; and Hotchkiss M1909 light machine guns advanced with the infantry to bring rapid fire against approaches. Mountain artillery was constrained by terrain and transport capacity and could not maintain the same volume of fire against distant targets as field guns. After crossing the Xijiang, the Guangdong Army did not simply push forward along one road. River transport brought troops into Wuzhou, from which formations expanded toward Hezhou and Pingle, forcing the Guangxi Army to cover both the eastern approaches and its rear toward Nanning. The Guangxi Army resisted from villages, mountain passes, and road junctions, avoiding a general engagement in open country, but this dispersion made it difficult to concentrate its brigades. The decisive development was not the destruction of one army in a single frontal battle. It was the revolt of Shen Hongying and Lin Hu inside Guangxi while the Guangdong Army pressed from the front. The fall of Nanning and the rear administrative centers deprived Lu Rongting of the means to concentrate his forces. Both sides suffered from long communication lines, fragmented command, and mixed weapons systems. Couriers, military reports, and rear-area telegraphs carried orders, but their speed was inadequate for sustained large-scale offensives. The result was a war of movement rather than a static trench struggle.
data: 可核對的時間框架是：1919年粵桂聯軍共同對付吳佩孚後，兩省關係由合作轉向戒備；1920年4月，邊界與西江中游衝突已發展為涉及多個師、旅的地區戰爭；4月至6月，粵軍沿西江下游向梧州施壓，同時由粵北經連州方向轉入桂東；6月至8月，戰線向賀縣、鐘山、平樂方向推進，桂軍在桂林、柳州一線的縱深受到牽動；夏末至初秋，陸榮廷失去有效指揮桂軍的條件；9月以後，重點轉為沈鴻英、林虎在南寧建立新軍政局面。主要運輸線有三條：其一由廣州經佛山、三水裝載，再沿西江經德慶、肇慶、封開、懷集至梧州；其二由梧州接駁，再沿賀縣、平樂方向進取；其三由廣州經韶關、連州，以山路和騾馬運輸接應桂東。廣三鐵路只能把後方補給送至三水，廣西中部沒有貫通鐵路，故彈藥多靠船運和人力背運；七九二毫米步槍彈與七五毫米炮彈不能互相替代，混合裝備增加分配難度。參戰規模可確定為雙方各投入數個師及若干旅，總量屬數萬人量級，但史料常把作戰、警戒和後勤人員混算，不能列為精確總數。傷亡數字同樣缺少一致口徑，本實錄不列未經核實的精確傷亡。
dataEn: The verifiable chronology begins with the Guangdong-Guangxi alliance against Wu Peifu in 1919, after which relations between the two provinces shifted from cooperation to mutual suspicion. By April 1920, fighting along the border and middle Xijiang had developed into a regional war involving several divisions and brigades. From April through June, the Guangdong Army pressed along the lower Xijiang toward Wuzhou while also turning from northern Guangdong through the Lianzhou area into eastern Guangxi. Between June and August, the front moved through the Hezhou, Zhongshan, and Pingle approaches, placing the Guilin-Liuzhou depth of Guangxi under pressure. By late summer or early autumn, Lu Rongting could no longer command the Guangxi field force effectively, and from September onward the principal issue became the establishment of a new military-political authority in Nanning by Shen Hongying and Lin Hu. Three supply corridors were of primary importance. The first ran from Guangzhou through Foshan and Sanshui, then by the Xijiang through Deqing, Gaoyao, Fengkai, and Huaiji to Wuzhou. The second continued from Wuzhou toward Hezhou and Pingle. The third ran north from Guangzhou through Shaoguan and Lianzhou to support operations in eastern Guangxi over mountain roads and by pack transport. The Guangzhou-Sanshui Railway could carry supplies only as far as Sanshui. With no continuous railway through central Guangxi, ammunition depended largely on river craft and human porters. The 7.92 mm rifle ammunition and 75 mm artillery shells were not interchangeable, and mixed inventories complicated distribution. The scale can safely be described as several divisions and several brigades per side, with overall participation in the tens of thousands. Contemporary sources often mixed combat troops, security detachments, and logistics personnel in their totals, so no precise overall strength should be claimed. Casualty figures likewise lack a consistent basis, and this account gives no unverified precise casualty total.
cause: 第一次粵桂戰爭的根源，是1919年前後共同敵人消失後，粵軍與舊桂系之間原有的軍事合作無法維持。護法運動失敗後，陳炯明、陸榮廷等地方軍政首長各自依靠省軍、稅收與地盤維持權力；兩省共同對付吳佩孚時，邊界矛盾尚可暫時擱置，吳佩孚退出粵北後，誰控制西江門戶與桂東山道便成為實際問題。梧州位於西江與桂江匯合處，向北可通賀縣、平樂、桂林，向南可扼制從廣州溯江而上的船運，既是廣西路線樞紐，也是兩省軍隊補給的交換點，因此其控制權遠比一條省界的實際爭奪重要。1920年春，桂軍在梧州及桂東邊境集結，粵軍也向西江下游調兵，具體的第一次直接碰撞在不同記述中日期不一，但很快由局部戒備升級為雙方全面動員。與此同時，沈鴻英、林虎反抗陸榮廷，使粵軍有機會借助廣西內部力量削弱舊桂系，而陸榮廷若失去南寧和後方資源，也難以長期維持對桂東前線的支援。這場戰爭不是以統一的政治綱領進行的國家統一戰爭，而是省級軍力、邊界利益、補給來源與領導權轉移同時交錯造成的區域戰爭。
causeEn: The deeper cause of the First Guangdong-Guangxi War was the inability of the Guangdong Army and the old Guangxi clique to preserve their military cooperation after their common external enemy had disappeared. After the Constitutional Protection Movement failed, local military-political leaders such as Chen Jiongming and Lu Rongting relied on provincial armies, local revenues, and territorial control to sustain their power. While the two provinces faced Wu Peifu together, boundary disputes could be deferred. Once Wu’s forces withdrew from northern Guangdong, control of the Xijiang gateway and the mountain routes into eastern Guangxi became a practical necessity. Wuzhou lay at the confluence of the Xijiang and Gui Rivers. Routes north ran toward Hezhou, Pingle, and Guilin, while the river carried shipping south toward Guangdong. It was therefore both a transport junction and the point at which the two provincial supply systems met, making its control more consequential than a conventional border dispute. In the spring of 1920, Guangxi troops concentrated around Wuzhou and the eastern border, while Guangdong also moved troops into the lower Xijiang. Sources do not agree on the date of the first direct collision, but local military precautions soon became a general mobilization by both sides. At the same time, Shen Hongying and Lin Hu revolted against Lu Rongting. This allowed Chen to weaken the old clique with the assistance of forces inside Guangxi, while Lu’s loss of Nanning and rear resources made prolonged support of the eastern front increasingly difficult. The conflict was not a national unification war conducted under a single political program. It was a regional war produced by the intersection of provincial military power, strategic routes, supply needs, and changing control relationships.
impact: 本役最直接的軍政後果，是陸榮廷失去作為廣西最高統帥的地位，舊桂系不再能以原有的省軍系統支配桂東、桂中與桂南。沈鴻英、林虎在南寧取得主導權後，廣西進入新桂系政治格局；但這個新格局依靠軍事首長間的臨時合作維持，並未形成中央化的省政機關。粵軍則因控制梧州及西江門戶而把影響力推入廣西，取得戰略要地與受援政權，卻同時背上遠距離 garrison、運輸和多套軍械的負擔。大量桂軍裝備在戰役中易手或散入其他省軍，舊桂系的各支人馬並未全被消滅，而以投降後整編、回鄉、附屬或轉投其他軍閥等方式延續。戰爭再次顯示北京政府無法直接恢復兩省秩序，地方軍隊的指揮、糧餉和補充只能依靠自身系統。這種結果並不穩固：不到一年，粵軍與取得廣西政權的新桂系又因控制權和指揮關係爆發第二次粵桂戰爭。一九二〇年的勝負因此首先改變了廣西的權力歸屬，也為陳炯明後來與孫中山及廣東內部其他力量之間的裂痕提供了軍力與地域條件，但它是重要背景，而不是一場戰爭即可造成的必然結果。
impactEn: The most immediate military and political consequence was Lu Rongting’s loss of his position as the supreme commander of Guangxi. The old clique could no longer dominate eastern, central, and southern Guangxi through its original provincial command system. After Shen Hongying and Lin Hu established themselves in Nanning, a new Guangxi political order emerged. It nevertheless rested on the temporary cooperation of regional military leaders rather than on a centralized provincial administration. The Guangdong Army, having secured Wuzhou and the Xijiang gateway, extended its effective influence into Guangxi. It gained strategic access and a dependent political ally, but it also inherited the burden of distant garrisons, long transport routes, and several incompatible weapons systems. Large quantities of Guangxi equipment changed hands during the campaign or dispersed into other provincial armies. The old clique’s formations were not annihilated; individuals continued through surrender and reorganization, return to their home districts, subsidiary service, or transfer to other regional armies. The fighting again demonstrated that the government in Beijing could not restore order directly in either province. Command, pay, and resupply remained functions of the provincial military systems. The outcome was unstable: within less than a year, the Guangdong Army and the new Guangxi authorities fought another Guangdong-Guangxi war over control and command relationships. The campaign of 1920 therefore first changed the ownership of political power in Guangxi and also supplied territorial and military conditions that later complicated relations among Chen Jiongming, Sun Yat-sen, and other forces in Guangdong. Those later developments were made more likely by the war, but were not the automatic result of a single campaign.
result: 到1920年夏末，陸榮廷已無法維持一支可與粵軍及廣西新勢力抗衡的統一野戰軍，桂東戰線首先失去主動，桂中與桂南的後方也因沈鴻英、林虎的起兵而分裂。陸榮廷隨後離開廣西的實際軍政位置；沈鴻英、林虎則在南寧建立新的廣西軍政中心，並以陳炯明的粵軍作為外部支援。粵軍取得的是戰役主動權與戰略門戶，而不是把廣西完整兼併：主力沒有建立對全省的永久行政接管，仍以扶植新桂系、維持西江影響和控制若干交通點為主要安排。舊桂軍也不是在全軍消滅中覆沒，其部隊由完整建制轉為分散、投降、整編或附屬於其他軍閥，陸榮廷的個人政治生命則在廣西基本結束。這是一場以省級權力重組和主要戰略要地易手為核心的結果。陳炯明一方取得明確的軍事勝利，新桂系取得廣西主導權；然而粵軍對廣西的介入越深，兩省未解決的指揮與利益衝突就越集中，這正是1921年第二次粵桂戰爭的直接前因。
resultEn: By the late summer of 1920, Lu Rongting could no longer maintain a unified field army capable of resisting both the Guangdong forces and the new Guangxi alignment. The eastern front lost initiative first, while the internal revolt of Shen Hongying and Lin Hu split the rear of central and southern Guangxi. Lu subsequently left his effective military and political position in Guangxi. Shen and Lin established a new military-political center at Nanning and relied on Chen Jiongming’s Guangdong Army for external support. What the Guangdong Army obtained was operational initiative and a strategic gateway, not a complete annexation of Guangxi. Its forces did not establish permanent administrative control over the entire province; the principal arrangement remained one of supporting the new Guangxi clique, preserving Guangdong influence along the Xijiang, and controlling selected transport points. The old Guangxi Army was not annihilated in a single destruction. Its formations became dispersed, surrendered, reorganized, or attached to other regional armies, while Lu Rongting’s effective political career in Guangxi effectively ended. The result was therefore centered on a realignment of provincial power and the transfer of major strategic locations. The side led by Chen Jiongming achieved a clear military victory, and the new Guangxi clique obtained control of Guangxi. At the same time, the deeper Guangdong intervention concentrated the unresolved questions of command and interest between the two provinces. Those unresolved issues became the immediate background to the Second Guangdong-Guangxi War of 1921.
